title: Container Task Priority Scheduling Sorter
real_world_story:
A cloud container cluster scheduler maintains a queue of N pending container tasks. Each task is defined by task_id, required cpu_cores, and required memory_gb. To ensure optimal placement for heavy computational workloads before cluster nodes fragment into small resource slivers, the scheduling engine prioritizes tasks with higher compute demands:
1. Primarily by cpu_cores descending.
2. Secondarily by memory_gb descending.
3. Tertiarily by task_id ascending.
problem_statement: Given N container tasks with task_id, cpu_cores, and memory_gb, sort the tasks according to the multi-criteria scheduling rules and output the ordered task IDs separated by a single space.
task: Sort container tasks by resource requirements and print the ordered task IDs separated by a single space.
input_format:
The first line contains a single integer N, the number of container tasks.
The next N lines each contain three space-separated integers: task_id, cpu_cores, and memory_gb.
output_format: Print the sorted sequence of task IDs on a single line, separated by a single space.

examples.explanation: Tasks 102 and 104 have 8 CPU cores; task 102 has 32 GB RAM, more than 104 (16 GB). Tasks 103 and 101 have 4 CPU cores; task 103 has 32 GB RAM, more than 101 (16 GB). Ordered task IDs: 102 104 103 101.
Both tasks have identical CPU (4) and RAM (16); tie-breaking by task_id places 10 before 20.

real_world_takeaway: Sorting multi-resource demands allows cluster orchestrators to pack heavy workloads first, mitigating cluster memory fragmentation.
